# Incident: T3 was taken over and used in a DDoS — 2026-10-03

**A dated record. Do not edit it.** The rules that came out of it live in the documents named under
"Where the lessons live", and those are the ones to change.

## In one paragraph

T3 was the Ghost 5 test server (`ghost5.inflozo.com`, Ghost 5.130.6, set up 2026-08-20). On 2026-10-03 an automated attacker
broke in without any of our keys:
1. It read an admin key out of Ghost's database through a public API.
2. It used that key to install a crafted theme.
3. The theme ran a program that joined a DDoS botnet.

DigitalOcean reported it on 2026-10-04. The owner retired T3 from testing (ruling **R-238**) and destroyed it. T1, Ghost
6.58.0, was checked the same day and is clean and not open to either flaw.

## What happened (UTC, read from T3's own logs)

| When | What |
|---|---|
| 2026-10-03 14:16 | IP 2.27.132.175 first looks at the site. |
| 14:31 – about 16:27 | **Blind SQL injection** through the Content API's `filter` on `/ghost/api/content/tags/`, using the site's public Content key. The payload was `slug:['\|\|CASE WHEN … THEN 0 ELSE EXP(710) END\|\|',archive]`, which reads `api_keys` one character at a time. |
| 16:27:52 | Ghost's `actions` log: the built-in **Zapier** integration uploads and activates the theme `lytojqclrosg`. Every Ghost has that integration and its Admin key; nobody created it. |
| 16:27:56 – 59 | It creates a page on the theme's template `page-irrwjorvicka` and opens it. The template is a `{{#get}}` whose filter holds a `__proto__`/`constructor` expression (**CVE-2026-22594**, open before Ghost 6.19.1). Opening the page runs `child_process`. |
| 16:28:00 – 03 | It re-activates `casper` and deletes the page. Deleting the theme fails. |
| 16:28:02 onward | Processes named `jb` and `jbd2/sda1-8` (posing as a kernel thread) run as the `ghost` user from `/var/tmp/w` (deleted). They connect to 23.95.228.20:1337, and the binary is re-dropped at `/tmp/kworker`. |
| 2026-10-04 | DigitalOcean reports the droplet in a DDoS of 43 droplets. |

**Ruled out:** SSH (password login off, one key, only the owner's IP in 30 days). Our keys: none of the Ghost 5 keys was
ever in the repository, and the Admin key used was Zapier's, not ours. Inflozo's servers: not involved.

**T1 checked the same day:** no foreign theme upload, no foreign actor in `actions`, no planted process, no code
injection. The attacker's own boolean pair (`1=1` against `1=0`) answered 200/500 on T3 (the control, open) and 200/200 on
T1 (not open).

## What we learnt

1. **An end-of-life Ghost on the public internet gets taken over.** Ghost 5 stopped getting fixes in January 2026, and T3
   lasted six weeks. Scanners try every public address all day, so "nobody knows it's there" protects nothing.
2. **A public key is still a door.** The Content key is public by design: it is in every page. One bug behind it was
   enough to read the whole database.
3. **A database read is an admin login.** Every Ghost install carries built-in integrations, such as Zapier, with Admin
   keys nobody created. Rotating *our* keys would not have helped.
4. **A pinned version is a frozen version.** The project pins T1 at 6.58.0 so measurements stay comparable (AD-34). That
   pin has to be checked against Ghost's security advisories, or it ages into T3.
5. **The theme is the weapon.** Inflozo writes `{{#get}}` filters into customers' themes. A Handlebars expression inside one
   is a code-execution exploit on every Ghost before 6.19.1, which includes every Ghost 5 site Inflozo still supports.
6. **We heard last.** DigitalOcean noticed a day later, and nothing of ours was watching.
7. **The checks that worked.** The safety classifier refuses Claude's own SSH reads and injection tests on the test
   servers, even after the owner's go-ahead. Read-only scripts that the owner ran, writing to a file Claude then read,
   found the answer in four rounds. `tools/probe/server-triage.sh` is those scripts, kept.

## Where the lessons live

| Lesson | Where it is now enforced or kept |
|---|---|
| 1, 4 | `docs/project-context.md`, under "Test Ghost servers", which every BMAD skill loads |
| 1 | `tools/probe/provision-ghost.sh` header: a Ghost 5 box is short-lived and firewalled to the owner's IP |
| 1 | Story 15.7's Ghost 5 pass (DW-326): spin up, run, destroy the same day |
| 5 | `packages/section-runtime/src/ad36.test.ts`: the exact payload is an AD-36 vector, refused at emission and inert through the fold |
| 5 (customers) | Open question for the owner, not yet asked: should the connect wizard warn Ghost 5 sites? (R-238's entry) |
| 7 | `tools/probe/server-triage.sh` |
| all | Ruling R-238 in `reconcile-designs-decisions.md` |
